news.title: ‘Embrace the chaos’: Tuchel aims to harness England’s football culture
news.lede: Head coach says he must accept lack of control in games. ‘Deep down, English players … they go for it’. Thomas Tuchel has admitted there are times when he craves greater control in matches. But the England head coach feels the more chaotic, adrenaline-fuelled nature of the Premier League will remain his template as he targets glory at Euro 2028.

news.title: Bengaluru boy to represent Indian team at ISF World Cup in China
news.lede: Bengaluru: Shourya VA, a class 12 student from the city, has been selected to represent India at International School Sport Federation (ISF) Football World Cup 2026 (boys under-18), to be held in Suzhou, China, from Oct 17 to 26. The defensive midfielder earned a place in the 20-member International Schools Sports Organisation (ISSO) India playing squad after a rigorous selection process involving some of the country’s top school-level footballers. The tournament, sanctioned by ISSO, will bring together school football teams from across the world.“. Earning a spot in the national playing squad and representing India on a global platform is a dream come true,” said Shourya.

news.title: Tuchel should listen to ‘the 0.1%’ and learn from England’s World Cup mistakes | Jacob Steinberg
news.lede: Head coach is keen to focus on positives but Nations League squad hints at desire for greater tactical options. Thomas Tuchel should be listening to the 0.1%. As he unveiled his first England squad since the World Cup, he said 99.9% of supporters he bumped into did not talk about his substitutions during the Argentina game. According to him, the conversation is far more positive.

news.title: Ukraine National Amputee Football Team Qualifies for 2026 World Cup
news.lede: The Ukraine national amputee football team will compete at the WAFF Amputee Football World Cup in Mexico. Replacing Ireland in the tournament, Ukraine joins 23 other nations competing for the world title in San Juan de los Lagos from November 13 to November 22, according to the World Amputee Football Federation. We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field.

news.title: Mbappe ends Nike partnership to join Swiss brand On
news.lede: France's forward #10 Kylian Mbappe celebrates scoring his team's first goal during the 2026 World Cup football tournament third-place match between France and England at the Miami Stadium in Miami on July 18, 2026. PARIS - France captain Kylian Mbappe has signed with Swiss sportswear brand On, ending a long association with Nike that stretched back to the start of his career, the company announced on Friday. "Today, Swiss sportswear brand On announces its entry into football alongside football champion Kylian Mbappe, marking the beginning of the brand's journey into the world's biggest sport," read a company statement. On also announced that 1998 World Cup winner Thierry Henry had been appointed its football director.

news.title: Hans-Joachim Watzke reveals that he considered making Thomas Tuchel Germany coach after 2022 World Cup
news.lede: It seems Germany could have had a change in coach sooner after the 2022 FIFA World Cup. Hans-Joachim Watzke, vice-president of the German Football Association (DFB), revealed to Sky Sport (as captured by @iMiaSanMia) that after Germany’s group stage exit in Qatar, he had considered replacing then-national coach Hansi Flick with Thomas Tuchel. Tuchel was without a job at the time after being sacked by Chelsea. We were knocked out quite miserably in Qatar.

news.title: UEFA put pressure on Gianni Infantino by using failed World Cup plan against him
news.lede: UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin has called for a full review into FIFA's finances and demanded they share £4.5billion cash reserves. Ceferin has written a powerful letter to FIFA president Gianni Infantino suggesting the world governing body dips into its huge wealth and gives each 211 member associations £7.5million each. It is another step designed to put pressure on Infantino and also get clarity on FIFA's finances after the World Cup sell-off plan. UEFA are demanding Infantino stands down while insisting the sell-off plan highlighted the funds at their disposal and making it clear the associations will get cash whether Infantino remains in charge or not.

news.title: Patrick Vieira: Senegal job an 'absolute dream' for former Arsenal midfielder
news.lede: Patrick Vieira (right) says he will work "heart and soul" to achieve success with Senegal. Patrick Vieira says it is "an honour" to become Senegal head coach, with the decision to take the job "one from the heart". The 50-year-old was born in the West African nation but subsequently represented France as a player, winning the 1998 World Cup and the 2000 European Championship with Les Bleus. The former Arsenal midfielder spoke of his "immense pride" to begin his first international job, following stints with New York City, Nice, Crystal Palace, Strasbourg and Genoa, at his unveiling by the Teranga Lions on Friday.
